rationale: I designed a balanced robot with four sensors spread evenly across the front to improve line detection and reduce noise sensitivity. The sensor size is medium (0.012) to balance resolution and noise robustness. The wheel radius and track are moderate to provide stable turning and speed. Controller gains are tuned to moderate values (kp=0.9, ki=0.15, kd=0.05) to ensure responsive but stable control, avoiding oscillations. Sensor weights are set to negative on the left sensors and positive on the right sensors to steer correctly based on line position. The line loss strategy is set to 'search_left' to recover effectively when the line is lost. This design aims to generalize well across different track shapes by balancing sensor coverage, control responsiveness, and recovery behavior. The requested measurements will confirm if the robot completes the track efficiently with low error and stable steering.
